classification.attribution: Credit Erdős--Herzog--Piranian for the problem and component lemma. Record the March 2026 forum comment as earlier public provenance for a cubic-proof claim without treating it as verified literature. Credit Pendyala for the published degree-four theorem. Attribute the explicit minimal-critical-value normalization, Rouché lemma, and Lean consumer on disk to the local source without priority language.
classification.mathematical_interest: The proof is compact and structurally different from the degree-four smallest-enclosing-disk argument: the smaller critical value simultaneously supplies the scale, root-count condition, and safe-spoke hub.
classification.reusable_scope: Low-degree sparse normal forms in which critical-value inequalities control root location and exact radial identities turn small roots into contained paths.
classification.why_it_matters: It supplies a checkable complete cubic proof and a clean analytic/formal split, but the public story must emphasize mechanism and verification rather than degree frontier or priority.

primary_sources.title: Metric properties of polynomials
primary_sources.exact_anchor: Printed p. 139 / PDF p. 15, immediately before Problem 5, proves that one component contains at least two roots; Problem 5 asks for a path of length less than two joining two roots.
primary_sources.supports: The original problem and the component input used to choose a critical value below one.
primary_sources.does_not_support: A cubic theorem, the normalized polynomial $P_b$, or the safe-spoke identity.

primary_sources.title: A Degree-Four Lemniscate Path Theorem
primary_sources.author: Venkata Siddharth Pendyala
primary_sources.exact_anchor: PDF p. 1, Theorem 1 and Lemma 1, state the degree-four path theorem and four-point radial lemma; PDF p. 3, proof of Theorem 1, applies smallest-enclosing-disk normalization and the two radial arms.
primary_sources.supports: A public, stronger adjacent degree-specific theorem predating the local August source and a distinct radial-hub mechanism.
primary_sources.does_not_support: The present cubic critical-value normalization or a literal derivation of the cubic theorem.

public_provenance.exact_anchor: Comment dated 19 March 2026: 'ChatGPT gave a proof for cubic polynomials, but failed to do so for degree >= 4.' The page simultaneously reports no partial solution claimed in the comments.
public_provenance.supports: An earlier public claim that a cubic proof existed, sufficient to make first-proof language unsafe.
public_provenance.does_not_support: Correctness, identity with the local argument, priority of a durable theorem, or a citable proof text.

mechanism_comparison.local_cubic_method: Choose the smaller critical value, normalize to $P_b$, use the other critical value to enter a Rouché-stable two-root region, and consume two small roots through an exact safe-spoke identity.
mechanism_comparison.published_degree_four_method: Normalize the smallest enclosing disk of four roots and use a finite radial-arm selection lemma; no critical-value or Rouché argument appears in the theorem proof.
mechanism_comparison.formalization_split: The analytic root supply remains ordinary mathematics; Lean checks only the algebraic containment and strict metric fan-in once two small roots are given.
mechanism_comparison.remaining_throat: Higher degree lacks the sparse cubic identity, and the unrestricted problem remains open despite degree-four coverage.
